sections.h2: Who do you pay property tax to in Burnett County, WI?
sections.html:
Pay the first installment to your town or village treasurer, and pay everything after July 31 to the Burnett County Treasurer. The town or village contact information sits in the upper left corner of your tax bill.

That split follows s. 74.11(6), which sends payments made on or before January 31 to the local taxation district treasurer and every other payment to the county treasurer. The County Treasurer's page repeats it in plain terms: current-year real estate taxes by January 31 go to the town or village, and all real estate taxes after July 31 go to Burnett County.

Burnett County has no incorporated cities. Its 24 municipalities are 21 towns (Anderson, Blaine, Daniels, Dewey, Grantsburg, Jackson, LaFollette, Lincoln, Meenon, Oakland, Roosevelt, Rusk, Sand Lake, Scott, Siren, Swiss, Trade Lake, Union, Webb Lake, West Marshland and Wood River) and three villages (Grantsburg, Siren and Webster). Both Grantsburg and Siren appear as a town and as a village, so confirm which one is printed on your bill.

sections.h2: When are Burnett County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate taxes are due January 31, either as a single payment or as the first of two installments, and the second installment is due July 31 (s. 74.11(2)). A bill under $100 must be paid in full by January 31.

  • If a payment is not received within five working days after January 31, the whole unpaid balance is delinquent as of February 1.
  • If the second installment is not received within five working days after July 31, the balance is delinquent as of August 1.
  • When a due date falls on a weekend, the grace period ends at the close of business on the first Friday of the following month.

The next January 31, in 2027, is a Sunday, so the last day to pay on time is Friday, February 5, 2027. July 31, 2027 is a Saturday, which moves that cutoff to Friday, August 6, 2027.

Delinquent real property taxes are paid to the county treasurer, with interest and penalties charged back to the preceding February 1. A municipality may also adopt an ordinance allowing three or more installments, with at least half paid by April 30 and the rest by July 31 (s. 74.12). Look at your bill, or ask your town or village treasurer, to learn which schedule applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do you change the mailing address or get payment alerts in Burnett County?
sections.html:
Call the Real Property Lister at 715.349.2183 to change the address that appears on your tax bill. The county treasurer's page lists that number for address change questions.

The county is moving its records to Ascent Land Records software, and the treasurer's page offers a sign-up for text or email notices. The alerts cover four events: your tax bill is ready, a payment has been receipted, a postponement reminder is due, and delinquent taxes are due. Anyone selling a seasonal or inherited home from out of state should sign up so a bill sent to an old address does not go unnoticed.

The office also prepares and mails delinquent tax notices and postponed-tax reminders, issues tax certificates, administers the Lottery and Gaming Credit, and prepares tax settlements.

sections.h2: Who sets your assessment in Burnett County, and how do you appeal it?
sections.html:
Your town's or village's assessor sets your value, and the county is required to carry that value onto the roll. Burnett County's Land Services FAQ says that if you disagree with the value, you should contact the assessor for your municipality first. The municipality's page on the county website lists who that is.

A formal appeal goes to the local Board of Review, which meets once a year in a window of 45 days starting on the fourth Monday of April (s. 70.47). In a town, the supervisors and the clerk make up the board unless the town has adopted an ordinance creating another board. A village board uses the village president and clerk in the same way. At least one member must complete state training each year.

  • Tell the board clerk, in writing or orally, at least 48 hours before the first meeting that you plan to object.
  • File a written objection in the first two hours of that meeting. The Department of Revenue form is PA-115A.
  • Show your own estimate of land and improvement value and the information behind it.
  • Expect the board to treat the assessor's number as correct until you present evidence otherwise.

After a Board of Review decision, a court appeal by certiorari must start within 90 days of the notice. An excessive assessment claim under s. 74.37 goes to the municipality by January 31 of the year the tax is payable. The state's Guide for Property Owners covers both steps.

sections.h2: Which Burnett County office handles which question?
sections.html:
Property questions in Burnett County are split among the treasurer, the Real Property Lister, Land Services, the clerk and your town or village. This table matches the question to the office.

QuestionOfficeContact on county pages
Change a tax bill addressReal Property Lister715.349.2183
Pay after July 31 or pay delinquent taxesCounty TreasurerCounty Treasurer page
Dispute an assessed valueMunicipal assessorListed on each municipality's page
Land use permit, maps, zoning layerLand Services715-349-2109
Building permitYour townThe town that contains the parcel
Tax deed land for saleCounty Clerk715-349-2173

Source: Burnett County Land Services FAQ, County Treasurer and Tax Deed Land for Sale pages.

The county FAQ adds two helpful details. The long parcel number on a tax statement has 24 digits and starts with 07-. Owner and parcel records are searchable on the county's Beacon mapping site.

sections.h2: What happens to tax-delinquent land in Burnett County?
sections.html:
The County Treasurer issues tax certificates and applications for tax deeds, and land the county takes by tax deed is sold through the county. The Tax Deed Land for Sale page currently reports no auctions. Parcels listed on the Wisconsin Surplus online auction can be bought only through that site.

Some parcels are sold over the counter at the County Clerk's office, Room 150 of the Government Center in Siren, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Payment must be cash, check or money order made out to the Burnett County Treasurer. The county page says no over-the-counter properties are for sale at this time.

If you own a parcel with unpaid taxes and want to sell it privately, pay or settle the balance with the County Treasurer first so the sale can close cleanly.

sections.h2: What is Burnett County like for owners and sellers?
sections.html:
Burnett County sits in northwest Wisconsin along the Minnesota line, with Siren as the county seat. The St. Croix Chippewa Indians of Wisconsin hold reservation lands in the county and are its largest employer, and the U.S. Department of Agriculture classes the county as a high-recreation retirement destination. Wisconsin Highways 35, 48, 70, 77 and 87 serve it.

The Census Bureau counts 17,223 residents in July 2025, up 4.2 percent from the 2020 base. Residents 65 and older make up 35.5 percent of the population, and 85.9 percent of housing is owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $231,300, the median household income is $62,819, and the county's 821.56 square miles of land average about 20 people per square mile. Only 143 building permits were issued in 2025.

The 2020 Census counted 15,201 housing units in the county, with 50.7 percent of them vacant. If you own a home here and live elsewhere, set up the county's bill alerts and keep the Real Property Lister's number handy.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property taxes to in Burnett County?
faqs.a: Pay the first installment, due January 31, to your town or village treasurer. Pay the second installment due July 31 and any delinquent taxes to the Burnett County Treasurer. The local treasurer's contact information is printed in the upper left corner of the tax bill.

faqs.q: When are Burnett County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The full payment or first installment is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. A bill under $100 is due in full by January 31. A missed first installment makes the entire unpaid balance delinquent as of February 1 once the five-working-day grace period passes.

faqs.q: How do I change my tax bill address in Burnett County?
faqs.a: Call the Real Property Lister at 715.349.2183. The County Treasurer's page directs address change questions to that number. The treasurer's page also offers text and email alerts for new bills, receipted payments and delinquent notices.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my assessment in Burnett County?
faqs.a: Start with your municipal assessor, then use your town or village Board of Review. Give the clerk notice at least 48 hours before the first meeting and file a written objection in its first two hours. The board meets within 45 days beginning the fourth Monday of April.

faqs.q: Does Burnett County sell tax deed land?
faqs.a: Yes. Parcels the county holds by tax deed may be listed on the Wisconsin Surplus online auction, which is the only way to buy those parcels, or sold over the counter at the County Clerk's office. The county's page currently shows no auctions and no over-the-counter parcels.
